summary: A [Conseil national du Numerique](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended at the national digital week in August 2026 and has not been constituted.
developments:
The recommendation came out of the Semaine du Numerique on 1 August 2026, which produced a set of proposals framed around digital sovereignty ([recommendations](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)).

No council, founding text or membership is on record. The base holds no whole-of-government digital strategy for the country either, so the coordinating body and the plan it would coordinate are both absent.

summary: [Universal connectivity is targeted for 2030](2026-07-30-mali-semaine-numerique-panel-couverture-universelle-2030) on a roadmap drafted with two neighbours, and an [updated access strategy with a white-zone map](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended.
developments:
The target was set at the national digital week's opening panel on 30 July 2026, with a roadmap drafted alongside Burkina Faso and Niger ([target](2026-07-30-mali-semaine-numerique-panel-couverture-universelle-2030)).

The same week recommended an updated universal-access strategy carrying a white-zone map, which the base records as not existing ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete), [panel](2026-07-30-mali-semaine-numerique-panel-couverture-universelle-2030)). Without that map, neither the target's distance nor its cost can be stated.

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence strategy](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended at the national digital week in August 2026, with no draft published.
developments:
The recommendation is the whole of the record: no draft, no lead ministry and no timetable is published ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)).

The country has meanwhile adopted regional artificial-intelligence governance guidelines with five other francophone states and recommended a confederation protocol on the subject, so the governance work is running ahead of any national strategy to govern.

summary: A [data-management law](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended at the national digital week in August 2026, and nothing has been tabled.
developments:
The recommendation came out of the same sovereignty-framed set of proposals as the digital council and the startups law ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)).

No draft, sponsoring ministry or parliamentary stage is on record. Data governance in the country currently rests on the 2013 personal-data statute and the authority administering it, and not on any instrument covering government data as an asset.

summary: The [personal data protection law of 2013](2026-08-04-mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1000-dossiers-au-programme) has been in force since May 2013 as amended, and is the stated basis for the authority's sanctions.
developments:
The statute is in force and the data-protection authority cites it as the basis on which it fines and issues formal notices ([law](2026-08-04-mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1000-dossiers-au-programme)).

No amendment, implementing decree or consolidated text has entered the base since, so what can be established here is that the law is used rather than what it now says.

summary: [Francophone West African artificial-intelligence governance guidelines](2026-07-09-wearetech-six-francophone-ai-governance-framework) were adopted with five other states in July 2026, led by an advocacy organisation.
developments:
The guidelines were adopted on 9 July 2026 and announced at a global dialogue on artificial-intelligence governance ([guidelines](2026-07-09-wearetech-six-francophone-ai-governance-framework)).

They are the country's only artificial-intelligence governance instrument in force, they are regional rather than national, and they were led by an advocacy organisation rather than by a state. No domestic statute, decree or regulator on the subject is held.

summary: The [data-protection authority](2026-08-04-mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1000-dossiers-au-programme) opened its second 2026 session with more than 1,000 files, and has a [regional antenna](2025-12-05-lessor-apdp-segou-antenne) at Segou.
developments:
The session opened on 3 August 2026 with more than 1,000 files before it over ten days, against about 2,000 declaratory files under review a year earlier and one fine of five million francs with more than 100 formal notices issued in 2025 ([session](2026-08-04-mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1000-dossiers-au-programme), [caseload](2025-10-07-apanews-apdp-examine-2000-dossiers-baux)).

A regional antenna opened at Segou in December 2025 ([antenna](2025-12-05-lessor-apdp-segou-antenne)). No figures are published for sanctions issued or files cleared, so the workload is visible and the output is not.

Cooperation with the Beninese authority was agreed in April 2025 with no joint action published since ([cooperation](2025-04-16-wearetech-benin-mali-data-protection-cooperation)).

summary: The authority [authorised the demobilisation commissions](2026-08-18-gouvernement-ml-cnddr-cni-formation-donnees-personnelles-ddr) to process ex-combatant data, and has a [mandatory lease-declaration decree](2025-10-07-apanews-apdp-examine-2000-dossiers-baux) in draft.
developments:
The national health insurance body completed a digital security training dedicated to data protection ([report](2026-08-29-malijet-protection-des-donnees-la-canam-cloture-une-formation)).

The two national demobilisation and integration commissions were authorised to collect and process ex-combatant and beneficiary data, and ran a three-day training on personal-data protection in domestic law covering it in August 2026; the authorisation's scope, retention period and the number of records held are not published ([authorisation](2026-08-18-gouvernement-ml-cnddr-cni-formation-donnees-personnelles-ddr)).

A draft decree making lease declaration mandatory was before the authority in October 2025 and no adoption is on record ([decree](2025-10-07-apanews-apdp-examine-2000-dossiers-baux)). Prior authorisation of a named sensitive processing is the strongest readiness signal the base holds for the country.

summary: Mali was [re-elected to the African Telecommunications Union board](2026-07-29-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-30) for 2027-2031, its data-protection authority [signed a confederation coordination roadmap](2025-11-21-digitalbusiness-aes-feuille-route-protection-donnees), and it remains a [Smart Africa member](2026-03-10-techafricanews-mali-smart-africa-mwc2026).
developments:
Re-election to the union board for the 2027-2031 term was recorded at the Abuja plenipotentiary in July 2026 ([re-election](2026-07-29-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-30)).

The Ouagadougou declaration on the digital economy was adopted at a regional salon in July 2026, recommending that member governments put digital at the centre of national strategies; Mali spoke for the three confederation states ([declaration](2026-08-07-communique-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-vendredi-7-aout-2026-mali)).

Membership of the continental smart-cities and connectivity body continues, with skills, cross-border fibre and a possible summit discussed at a ministerial meeting in March 2026 ([membership](2026-03-10-techafricanews-mali-smart-africa-mwc2026)).

2025-11-18 - the three confederation data-protection authorities [signed an operational roadmap for their coordination framework](2025-11-21-digitalbusiness-aes-feuille-route-protection-donnees), the first practical confederation-level mechanism on the record for cross-border personal-data governance; no budget, secretariat or first joint action is published.

progress: Mixed, a confederation protocol recommended while ECOWAS instruments lapse
summary: A [confederation protocol on artificial-intelligence governance](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended in August 2026 with no text, while [ECOWAS membership ended](2025-01-29-ecowas-withdrawal-press-statement) in January 2025.
developments:
The recommendation was one of the national digital week's sovereignty proposals ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)).

No text, negotiating mandate or signature is on record. The country's harmonisation work that has actually happened runs through travel and identity document specifications agreed with the same two states, which the base records separately.

2025-01-29 - ECOWAS's own statement records that [withdrawal became effective that day](2025-01-29-ecowas-withdrawal-press-statement), setting out only narrow transitional arrangements - passports, trade treatment under the liberalisation scheme, free movement and cooperation with ECOWAS officials - and leaving the post-withdrawal applicability of ECOWAS legal-harmonisation instruments, digital and data-governance acts among them, unresolved.

progress: Regressed, cybercrime provisions used to prosecute a journalist while a ministerial instruction directs prosecutors at platform content
summary: A [newspaper editor was sentenced](2026-08-20-ipi-mali-cybercrime-provisions-target-journalists) before the cybercrime pole, and a [ministerial instruction](2026-07-30-mali-justice-reseaux-sociaux-instruction-parquets) directs prosecutors at social-media content.
developments:
The editor was arrested in June by the national cybercrime unit and sentenced to twelve months with six suspended for undermining the credibility of the state; a press-freedom body describes authorities using cybercrime provisions to prosecute journalists ([sentence](2026-08-20-ipi-mali-cybercrime-provisions-target-journalists), [case](2026-08-03-lessor-journaliste-chahana-takiou-condamne-pole-cybercriminalite)). Neither the judgment nor the charging instrument is held, and the characterisation of a pattern is that body's.

The justice ministry instructed prosecutors on 29 July 2026 to act on platform content, building on existing penal and cybercrime provisions with no new statute ([instruction](2026-07-29-mali-communique-ministre-justice-depravation-reseaux-sociaux), [account](2026-07-30-mali-justice-reseaux-sociaux-instruction-parquets)).

A survey of 2,220 adults in April 2026 puts a short-video platform third among main news sources at 19.7 per cent, behind radio at 27.3 and television at 21.7 ([survey](2026-07-01-fes-mali-metre-2026), [reporting](2026-08-20-maliweb-mali-metre-2026-reseaux-sociaux-information)).

summary: A civil-society organisation launched a [citizen application for reporting and checking online content](2026-08-24-mali-women-tech-app-against-disinformation) in August 2026, closing a campaign it says reached 68,885 people.
developments:
The application is aimed at young people and civil-society organisations, and was launched alongside the closing report of a digital campaign against viral falsehood that the organisation says reached 68,885 people ([launch](2026-08-24-mali-women-tech-app-against-disinformation)).

The work is funded through a foreign-ministry facility with support from the ministry responsible for the digital economy, so it is civil-society delivery inside a state relationship rather than independent of it. No user or report-volume figure is published.

progress: Mixed, the universal access fund's budget cut by a third in July while it signed four-year school connection commitments
summary: The universal access fund's 2026 budget was [cut 32 per cent](2026-07-26-mali-agefau-11e-conseil-administration-budget-revise) in July, days after it signed [conventions to connect every secondary school](2026-07-26-mali-agefau-conventions-education-emploi-numerique) by end-2027.
developments:
The fund's adopted 2026 budget of FCFA 41,151,471,000 was revised down to FCFA 27,886,688,000 on 23 July 2026, after 8 per cent of the annual budget was spent in the first half and receipts ran at 56 per cent of forecast ([revision](2026-07-26-mali-agefau-11e-conseil-administration-budget-revise)).

The day before, it signed two four-year renewable conventions with the education and employment ministries committing it to connect every secondary, technical and vocational school by the end of 2027, with cumulative education spend put above FCFA 17bn ([conventions](2026-07-26-mali-agefau-conventions-education-emploi-numerique), [partnership](2026-07-23-mali-agefau-partenariat-education-emploi-lepays)).

The fund sits under direct prime-ministerial tutelle and named a new director-general the same week; a named-analyst investigation dates its removal from the regulator to 2012 ([governance](2026-07-26-mali-agefau-11e-conseil-administration-budget-revise), [investigation](2026-07-27-maliweb-fonds-acces-universel-captation-agefau)).

summary: An [EUR 80m development-bank loan](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre) funds 4G and fibre build, and [FCFA 88,740,927 of ICT equipment](2026-08-04-lunesco-remet-des-equipements-informatiques-au-ministere-de-leducation-nationale-mali) went to eight teacher-training institutes.
developments:
The loan was signed in November 2025, co-invested with a regional bank and a private-sector window, and covers 300 4G towers, half of them rural, and fibre to about 300,000 households ([loan](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre)).

Equipment worth FCFA 88,740,927 was handed to eight teacher-training institutes on 30 July 2026, funded by Japan and implemented by a United Nations agency, with no maintenance, connectivity or software provision stated ([handover](2026-08-04-lunesco-remet-des-equipements-informatiques-au-ministere-de-leducation-nationale-mali), [account](2026-07-31-mali-des-equipements-numeriques-remis-a-huit-instituts-de-formation-des-maitres)).

summary: The only private commitment naming the country is a [US$6bn connectivity pledge](2024-03-01-niger-e-and-partner2connect-commitment-thenationalnews) spread undivided across sixteen markets.
developments:
A Gulf operator pledged US$6bn to an international connectivity coalition for 2024 to 2026 across sixteen markets including Mali, undivided between them ([pledge](2024-03-01-niger-e-and-partner2connect-commitment-thenationalnews)).

No Mali-specific allocation is published, so the base can record that the country is named in a large commitment and not what share of it, if any, reaches the country.

summary: A [development-bank loan](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre) of November 2025 puts 300 4G towers, half of them rural, and fibre to about 300,000 households into build.
developments:
The build is the base's only forward commitment on mobile coverage: 300 towers with half in rural areas, alongside fibre to about 300,000 households ([loan](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre)).

No subscriber count, penetration rate or coverage share is published for the country at all, so the addition is on record and the base it adds to is not.

progress: No change, a first published comparison with no earlier price series behind it
summary: About [1.5GB of mobile data in Bamako costs what buys 25GB in Dakar](2026-08-14-mali-telecom-data-affordability-senegal-comparison), and the market has [one surviving independent provider](2026-07-27-maliweb-fonds-acces-universel-captation-agefau).
developments:
The comparison, published in August 2026, puts the ratio at roughly twenty-five to one and attributes it to weak market oversight, the duopoly of the two incumbent operators and the years since a new operator licence was issued ([comparison](2026-08-14-mali-telecom-data-affordability-senegal-comparison)). It is a press comparison rather than a tariff series, and neither the basket nor the date of the prices compared is stated.

One independent internet service provider is reported surviving, buying wholesale transit at near-retail prices, which is the wholesale structure behind the retail figure ([provider](2026-07-27-maliweb-fonds-acces-universel-captation-agefau)).

summary: Retail [fibre speeds doubled to 100 Mbps across six cities](2026-06-15-ecofin-moov-africa-doubles-fibre-ai-assistant-mia), [ADSL is to be retired](2026-07-23-malitel-adsl-ftth) by end-2026, and a [single national transport operator](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended.
developments:
An operator doubled fibre speeds at no extra cost in June 2026, reaching up to 100 Mbps across six cities ([speeds](2026-06-15-ecofin-moov-africa-doubles-fibre-ai-assistant-mia)).

Retirement of copper and migration to fibre to the home was announced for the end of 2026, with no subscriber or coverage figure published ([migration](2026-07-23-malitel-adsl-ftth)).

The national digital week recommended making the state transport-infrastructure company the sole national operator of transport infrastructure, as a law; nothing has been tabled ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)). No route map or backbone length for the country is held.

summary: An [independent subsea route with automated rerouting](2026-07-15 CSquared boosts internet by integrating with 2Africa West cable) was added behind the inland backbone in July 2026, easing a landlocked country's exposure to three landing points.
developments:
The inland backbone integrated capacity on a west-coast subsea system in July 2026, giving an independent route with automated rerouting behind it ([integration](2026-07-15 CSquared boosts internet by integrating with 2Africa West cable)).

The country's inland routes had been exposed to the concentration of landings at Abidjan, Accra and Lagos. The account is the vendor's, and no capacity, price or utilisation figure is published.

progress: Mixed, a licensed operator's satellite service reaching remote residents while unauthorised terminals are seized
summary: An operator's [satellite 3G and 4G service](2025-05-07-techafricanews-orange-mali-intelsat-4g-satellite) reaches about 360,000 remote residents, while the regulator is [seizing unauthorised terminals](2026-07-02-amrtp-controle-saisie-wifi-zone-starlink-talkie-walkie) nationwide.
developments:
The satellite-backhauled service is in service reaching about 360,000 remote residents, with no later coverage figure published ([service](2025-05-07-techafricanews-orange-mali-intelsat-4g-satellite), [loan](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre)).

A six-month lifting of the import ban on low-orbit kits was reported in October 2024 ([lifting](2024-10-10-mali-starlink-levee-interdiction-voa)), the prohibition on unauthorised equipment was restated in March 2026 with a warning of sanctions ([prohibition](2026-03-13-amrtp-rappelle-interdiction-starlink-wifi-zone)), and control, seizure and dismantling operations were announced in June 2026 against unauthorised kits, shared Wi-Fi zones and walkie-talkies, with operators ordered to cease immediately ([enforcement](2026-07-02-amrtp-controle-saisie-wifi-zone-starlink-talkie-walkie)). Imports and use remain banned pending authorisation.

summary: A [Tier III national data centre](2026-02-05 Government of Mali launches data center in Bamako) was inaugurated in Bamako in January 2026, hosting state data and framed to carry mutualised regional infrastructure.
developments:
The centre entered service on 31 January 2026 with stated availability of 99.982 per cent ([launch](2026-02-05 Government of Mali launches data center in Bamako), [opening](2026-02-02 Mali opens Tier III data center in Bamako amid regional push to keep data at home)).

It hosts state data and is framed as able to carry mutualised infrastructure for the three confederation states ([account](2026-02-02 Mali unveils modern Tier III data centre)). No capacity in racks or megawatts, no customer count and no commercial facility elsewhere in the country is recorded.

summary: [Diesel-to-solar conversion of network sites](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre) is inside the November 2025 operator loan, with no site count published.
developments:
The conversion is in the loan's scope and is the base's only record of power provision for digital infrastructure in the country ([loan](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre)).

No site count, generation figure, outage measure or grid-availability statistic is published, so what the network runs on can be described in kind and not in quantity.

summary: The state technology agency administers the [country-code domain](2025-12-30-lessor-agetic-intranet-point-ml), which held 13,441 names across thirty registrars at the end of 2025.
developments:
The registry held 13,441 domain names across thirty registrars in December 2025, administered by the state agency that also builds the government intranet and the justice e-services recorded elsewhere in this ledger ([registry](2025-12-30-lessor-agetic-intranet-point-ml)).

That agency is the whole of the state's recorded in-house capability. No technical headcount, maintenance arrangement or statement of which systems the state can run without a vendor is held.

summary: A [National Cybersecurity Strategy 2026-2030](2025-12-09-wearetech-mali-strategie-cybersecurite-2026-2030) was adopted in December 2025, an [agency created](2026-07-01-maliactuel-anssi-agence-cybersecurite-creee) to implement it, and a [criminal chamber](2026-05-21-lessor-cybercrime-chamber-operational) began hearing cases.
developments:
The strategy was adopted by the Council of Ministers on 9 December 2025 ([strategy](2025-12-09-wearetech-mali-strategie-cybersecurite-2026-2030)).

The information-systems security agency was created by Council of Ministers texts in June 2026 to implement it, with no budget or staffing published ([agency](2026-07-01-maliactuel-anssi-agence-cybersecurite-creee)).

The criminal chamber of the national cybercrime pole began hearing cases on 21 May 2026, opening with four cases and eight accused ([chamber](2026-05-21-lessor-cybercrime-chamber-operational)). The same pole is the venue in which a journalist was prosecuted, so the institutional build and the speech concern recorded elsewhere in this ledger are the same machinery.

summary: A [government intranet](2025-12-30-lessor-agetic-intranet-point-ml) had thirteen services integrated at the end of 2025, and a [national public key infrastructure](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended for deployment.
developments:
The intranet had thirteen services integrated in December 2025, with a draft decree to make government messaging mandatory ([intranet](2025-12-30-lessor-agetic-intranet-point-ml)).

Effective deployment of a national public key infrastructure and electronic signature services was recommended at the national digital week, with no first service named ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)). Between them these are an internal network and an intention, not an exchange: no transaction volume, service catalogue or connected-agency count is held.

summary: Five document categories are issued on the [confederation biometric passport](2026-07-21-lesahel-editorial-passeports-biometriques-aes) to international specification, under [specifications validated](2024-11-22-aes-communique-final-specifications-documents-voyage-identite) by three security ministers.
developments:
The three states' security ministers validated harmonised travel and identity document specifications at Bamako in November 2024 and referred them to the heads of state ([specifications](2024-11-22-aes-communique-final-specifications-documents-voyage-identite), [validation](2024-11-23-mali-ministere-securite-aes-validation-specifications-bamako)).

The common biometric passport launched in January 2025 ([launch](2025-01-27 Sahel states under military rule unveil common biometric passport Jan. 29)) and five categories are now issued to international civil aviation specification on a five-year, thirty-four-page book ([categories](2026-07-21-lesahel-editorial-passeports-biometriques-aes), [supplier](2025-10-28 Mali Launches 'E-AES' Biometric Passport, Taps China's Emptech in Digital Sovereignty Move)). No issuance count, rejection rate or verification figure is published.

summary: The [confederation biometric identity card](2026-06-02-afriktimes-aes-cib-aes-diaspora-pilot-bamako) was piloted on Malian soil in June 2026 for another member state's residents, with no Malian enrolment figure published.
developments:
The cross-border diaspora enrolment pilot ran in Bamako in June 2026, enrolling Burkinabe residents rather than Malian citizens ([pilot](2026-06-02-afriktimes-aes-cib-aes-diaspora-pilot-bamako)).

No Malian enrolment figure, coverage share or rollout date is published, so the country's first biometric identity card operation on record served somebody else's population.

progress: Mixed, a national agency created for document security while passport supply moved from one foreign vendor to another
summary: A [national agency for civil status document security](2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps) was created in 2025, and passport supply [moved from a French to a Chinese vendor](2025-10-28 Mali Launches 'E-AES' Biometric Passport, Taps China's Emptech in Digital Sovereignty Move) in October 2025.
developments:
The agency was created in 2025 with no output figure published ([agency](2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps)).

The passport supplier changed from Idemia of France to Emptech of China in October 2025, a change officials cast as regained sovereignty and local data management ([supplier](2025-10-28 Mali Launches 'E-AES' Biometric Passport, Taps China's Emptech in Digital Sovereignty Move)).

Neither move puts the credential's production in national hands: what the base records is a domestic body responsible for security and a foreign body responsible for supply.

summary: The [NINA national identity number](2026-02-12-maliweb-justice-casier-nationalite-en-ligne) is in use as the national identity key and authenticates applications to the justice e-services.
developments:
The number is the identity key on which the online criminal record and nationality certificate applications are made ([number](2026-02-12-maliweb-justice-casier-nationalite-en-ligne)).

No count of systems keyed on it, no authentication volume and no coverage share of the population holding one is published, so its reach into other systems is recorded by example and not by measure.

summary: A [bank-channel pilot for pension payment](2026-07-28-mali-digitalisation-sante-developpement-social-cmss) completed in July 2026 and is reported ready for phased extension to other partner banks.
developments:
Mobile pension payment was already live; the bank-channel pilot with one partner bank completed on 27 July 2026 and is reported ready for phased extension ([pilot](2026-07-28-mali-digitalisation-sante-developpement-social-cmss)).

No pensioner count, payment volume or extension date is published. It is the only government-to-person payment stream recorded for the country.

summary: [TresorPay](2025-03-20-wearetech-tresorpay-guichet-unique-foncier) takes identity fees and fines, and about [FCFA 200m was collected digitally at civil registry centres](2026-07-31-mali-collectivites-digitalisation-paiements-etat-civil) between July 2024 and May 2026.
developments:
The treasury payment service launched in March 2025 for identity fees and fines, with no transaction figure published ([service](2025-03-20-wearetech-tresorpay-guichet-unique-foncier)).

About FCFA 200m was collected at civil registry centres between July 2024 and May 2026, and every local authority has been ordered to report within thirty days ([collections](2026-07-31-mali-collectivites-digitalisation-paiements-etat-civil)). That reporting order is the base's only sign that the state is measuring what its own digital channels take.

summary: Both mobile money operators now issue prepaid cards: [one launched in June 2025](2025-06-11-maliweb-orange-money-orabank-mastercard-prepaid) with transaction caps, the [second in April 2026](2026-04-09-le360-moov-money-mali-carte-prepayee-mastercard-gitex).
developments:
The first telco-led prepaid card launched with a bank partner in June 2025, capped at two million francs a transaction and ten million a month ([first card](2025-06-11-maliweb-orange-money-orabank-mastercard-prepaid)).

The second launched at a regional technology exhibition in April 2026 ([second card](2026-04-09-le360-moov-money-mali-carte-prepayee-mastercard-gitex)). No issuance, activation or spend figure is published for either, so what the base records is that the wallet has acquired a card rail and not how much travels on it.

progress: Mixed, transaction volume growing while the country's share of the union fell and the distributor network contracted sharply
summary: The country's [share of union electronic-money value fell to 11.7 per cent](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024) in 2024, and its [distributor network fell 46.34 per cent](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024), the steepest in the union.
developments:
Share of union transaction value fell from 12.1 per cent in 2023 to 11.7 per cent in 2024, and share of volume stood at 10.7 per cent, on volume growth of 18.58 per cent and 7.29 per cent of accounts opened ([shares](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024)).

Distributor numbers fell 46.34 per cent in 2024, the steepest fall in the union ([network](2026-01-01-bceao-services-financiers-numeriques-uemoa-2024)). Volume rising while the agent network halves is the shape worth watching here: it is consistent with use concentrating on fewer, larger points rather than spreading.

summary: A [remittance integration into mobile wallets](2025-05-29 TerraPay enables cross-border remittances for Wave Mobile Money users in Mali) was announced in May 2025 and no volume has been published since.
developments:
The integration between a cross-border payments network and a wallet operator was announced in May 2025, vendor-reported ([integration](2025-05-29 TerraPay enables cross-border remittances for Wave Mobile Money users in Mali)).

No corridor, volume, price or count of participating institutions is published, and no regional switch connection for the country is separately recorded.

summary: A [national digital directory of diaspora skills](2026-08-24-mali-digital-directory-diaspora-skills-launched) was launched in Washington in August 2026, with no data-protection basis stated.
developments:
The directory registers professional profiles across economic, administrative, academic, private-sector and emerging fields so that ministries can identify expertise against specific needs; it is run by the embassy to the United States and was launched on 22 August 2026 ([launch](2026-08-24-mali-digital-directory-diaspora-skills-launched)).

The minister described it as an accreting database whose usefulness depends on take-up and on profiles being kept current. Questions at the ceremony went to registration terms and to how the recorded data would be used, and no data-protection basis is stated.

progress: Mixed, birth registration near ninety per cent against death registration near twenty, on a village ledger still kept by hand
summary: [Birth registration stands at 89.5 per cent](2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps) across 747 functional centres while [death registration is about 20 per cent](2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps), and the [village register](2026-07-24-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-29) remains hand-kept.
developments:
Birth registration was recorded at 89.5 per cent across 747 functional primary centres in mid-2025, with no later figure published ([births](2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps)).

Death registration stood at about 20 per cent on the same account ([deaths](2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps)). A civil register that captures nine births in ten and one death in five cannot support the population arithmetic that other systems would draw on.

The village census ledger from which family record books are issued was formalised in a draft ordinance adopted in July 2026, replacing a 2006 statute, and remains a hand-kept ledger ([ordinance](2026-07-24-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-29)).

summary: A [land information system and one-stop land office](2025-03-20-wearetech-tresorpay-guichet-unique-foncier) launched in March 2025 and no transaction figure has been published.
developments:
The system and the one-stop office launched together on 18 March 2025 ([launch](2025-03-20-wearetech-tresorpay-guichet-unique-foncier)).

No parcel count, transaction figure, coverage area or link to the payment service launched the same day is published, so the base records that the office exists and not what passes through it.

summary: A [national digital health portal](2026-07-08-techgriot-mali-national-digital-health-portal) launched in July 2026, a [health information system](2025-09-17 Mali rolls out new digital tools to modernize public administration) is in build, and a [unique patient identifier](2026-07-28-mali-digitalisation-sante-developpement-social-cmss) runs in one hospital.
developments:
The portal went live on 8 July 2026 under the health digital plan, with facility geolocation; power, the urban-rural divide and interoperability were flagged as obstacles at launch ([portal](2026-07-08-techgriot-mali-national-digital-health-portal)).

The health information system is in build and is stated to link to the national identity number and to mandatory health insurance ([system](2025-09-17 Mali rolls out new digital tools to modernize public administration), [platforms](2025-09-26 Mali introduces new platforms to enhance digital public service access)).

A unique patient identifier runs an end-to-end digitised circuit in one Bamako hospital across registration, laboratory, consultation and pharmacy ([identifier](2026-07-28-mali-digitalisation-sante-developpement-social-cmss)). One hospital is the extent of the working evidence.

summary: [Online criminal records and nationality certificates](2026-02-12-maliweb-justice-casier-nationalite-en-ligne) went live in February 2026, keyed on the national identity number with an authenticity check.
developments:
The services launched during a justice week in February 2026, with applications keyed on the national identity number and an authenticity check on the issued document ([services](2026-02-12-maliweb-justice-casier-nationalite-en-ligne)).

They were built by the state technology agency. No application volume, issuance count or processing time is published, and no case-management system for the courts themselves is recorded.

summary: A [pilot exchanging transit-goods data with Ivorian customs](2026-08-13-mali-customs-interconnection-cote-divoire-pilot) is running, presented at a Bamako roundtable in August 2026.
developments:
The customs administration frames the pilot as cutting fraud and transit delays, and gives no completion date for the full interconnection ([pilot](2026-08-13-mali-customs-interconnection-cote-divoire-pilot), [roundtable](2026-08-07-mali-trade-facilitation-customs-interconnection)).

No counterpart administration, timetable, cost or system name is stated in the record held. For a landlocked economy whose imports move through a neighbour's ports, this is the single most consequential exchange in the ledger and the least documented.

summary: A [diaspora services platform](2025-02-21 Mali Launches Digital Platform to Streamline Services for Its Diaspora), a [driving licence and vehicle registration service](2025-09-17 Mali rolls out new digital tools to modernize public administration), a [territorial administration system](2025-09-17 Mali rolls out new digital tools to modernize public administration) and an [HR management system](2026-07-24-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-29) are the recorded stack.
developments:
The diaspora services platform launched in February 2025 with no usage figure published ([platform](2025-02-21 Mali Launches Digital Platform to Streamline Services for Its Diaspora)).

The driving licence and vehicle registration service is live and linked to the treasury payment service and the customs system ([service](2025-09-17 Mali rolls out new digital tools to modernize public administration), [presentation](2025-09-26 Mali introduces new platforms to enhance digital public service access)), while the territorial administration data management system is in build with no deployment figure ([territorial system](2025-09-17 Mali rolls out new digital tools to modernize public administration)).

An integrated human resources management system was reported in build in July 2026, with no scope or completion figure published ([human resources](2026-07-24-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-29)). Not one of the four carries a usage number.

summary: One commune is running a [fiscal census and financial-management digitisation](2026-08-13-mali-koutiala-fiscal-census-digitalization) to widen its own-source revenue, funded by a foreign embassy.
developments:
The programme surveys taxable commercial equipment and public-space use and equips the town hall with digital financial-management tools ([programme](2026-08-13-mali-koutiala-fiscal-census-digitalization)).

It is funded by an embassy and run with a non-governmental organisation, with no budget, timetable or revenue target stated. It is the only local-government digitisation on record for the country, in one commune.

summary: A state [artificial-intelligence and robotics centre](2026-08-01-lessor-semaine-numerique-cloture-transformation-digitale) demonstrated a locally built intrusion-detection technology, and an operator [launched an assistant](2026-06-15-ecofin-moov-africa-doubles-fibre-ai-assistant-mia) in June 2026.
developments:
The centre is operating and has one demonstration on record, of a locally built intrusion-detection technology shown on 1 August 2026 ([centre](2026-08-01-lessor-semaine-numerique-cloture-transformation-digitale)).

An operator launched an artificial-intelligence assistant in June 2026, operator-reported ([assistant](2026-06-15-ecofin-moov-africa-doubles-fibre-ai-assistant-mia)). Neither carries a model description, dataset or evaluation, and no national language model for the country's languages is recorded.

summary: The state [raised its holding in the incumbent operator from 49 to 56 per cent](2026-06-25-businessinsider-mali-regains-sotelma-majority-stake) for FCFA 160bn in June 2026, cutting the foreign partner to a minority.
developments:
The purchase took the state to 56 per cent, put the foreign partner into a minority and came with a licence renewal ([purchase](2026-06-25-businessinsider-mali-regains-sotelma-majority-stake)); it is about US$277m and comes seventeen years after the 2009 privatisation ([purchase](2026-06-25-businessinsider-mali-regains-sotelma-majority-stake)).

It is the largest single act on the country's digital industry in the base, and it is a change of ownership rather than of capability: no manufacturing, software export or domestic supplier capacity is separately recorded.

summary: A [startups law](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete) was recommended at the national digital week in August 2026, and nothing has been tabled.
developments:
The recommendation sits alongside the digital council and the data-management law in the same set of sovereignty proposals ([recommendation](2026-08-03-mali-semaine-du-numerique-recommandations-souverainete)).

No draft, definition of a startup, register or count of firms is held for the country, so the base records an intention to create a legal status and no measure of the population it would apply to.

summary: [Computer equipment worth FCFA 88,740,927](2026-08-04-lunesco-remet-des-equipements-informatiques-au-ministere-de-leducation-nationale-mali) was handed to eight teacher-training institutes in July 2026, with no maintenance or connectivity provision stated.
developments:
The handover to eight institutes took place on 30 July 2026, funded by Japan and implemented by a United Nations agency ([handover](2026-08-04-lunesco-remet-des-equipements-informatiques-au-ministere-de-leducation-nationale-mali), [account](2026-07-31-mali-des-equipements-numeriques-remis-a-huit-instituts-de-formation-des-maitres)).

No maintenance, connectivity or software provision is stated, and no curriculum, teacher count or pupil-facing programme is recorded, so the country's school-level digital capacity is on record as hardware delivered to trainers.

summary: A [digital university strategic framework](2024-05-10-unesco-universite-numerique-du-mali-cadre-strategique) was validated in May 2024 for 132,186 students across sixteen institutions, at an 81 to 1 student-teacher ratio.
developments:
The framework and action plan were validated on 7 May 2024, against 132,186 students across sixteen higher-education institutions and a student-teacher ratio of 81 to 1, well outside the international norm of 25 to 1 ([framework](2024-05-10-unesco-universite-numerique-du-mali-cadre-strategique)).

No creation decree or launch date for the digital university has been published since that validation, so the instrument built to relieve the ratio has not itself been created.

summary: A [digital-skills programme for 15,000 young people](2026-08-01-lessor-semaine-numerique-cloture-transformation-digitale) opened first-cohort recruitment in August 2026, and an [operator centre placed 350 graduates](2026-07-22-orange-odc-350-graduates).
developments:
Recruitment for the first cohort opened on 1 August 2026 under a convention with a local association, targeting 15,000 young people ([programme](2026-08-01-lessor-semaine-numerique-cloture-transformation-digitale)).

An operator's digital centre reported 350 young people placed on the labour market by July 2026, operator-reported ([placements](2026-07-22-orange-odc-350-graduates)). One target and one company's figure are the whole of the labour-market evidence for the country.

summary: The base holds [no long-term national research strategic plan](2009-12-17-mali-document-politique-nationale-enseignement-superieur-recherche-scientifique), and the higher-education digital framework validated in 2024 is the nearest thing to one.
developments:
The national higher-education and scientific research policy document of 2009 is the base's oldest source for the country, and it records no long-term research strategic plan and a teacher-student ratio of one to a hundred at the main university ([policy](2009-12-17-mali-document-politique-nationale-enseignement-superieur-recherche-scientifique)).

No think tank, research centre or university department is recorded contributing to national digital policy, and the sovereignty proposals adopted in 2026 were produced by a government week rather than by any research body.

summary: A [women's digital-training target of 70 per cent by 2032](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre) was set inside the November 2025 operator loan, with no interim figure published.
developments:
The target was set as a condition of the development-bank loan rather than by the state ([target](2025-11-17-ifc-orange-mali-80m-loan-4g-fibre)).

No interim figure, baseline or sex-disaggregated measure of access, ownership or use is published for the country, so the only gender commitment in the base sits in a private financing agreement and has no measurement behind it.

summary: The statistics institute's [microdata archive holds 107 studies](2026-08-10-mali-instat-microdata-catalogue), and the [fifth population census](2024-04-01-iati-se-0-se-6-11793-11793a0201-mali-rgph5-census-special-review) was externally funded across three records.
developments:
The institute's own archive held 107 studies at capture in August 2026, led by the 2022 census and near-annual agricultural surveys running back to the late 1990s ([archive](2026-08-10-mali-instat-microdata-catalogue)).

External support to the fifth population and housing census runs across an original contribution and an agreement amendment from 2018 and a special review committed in April 2024 ([review](2024-04-01-iati-se-0-se-6-11793-11793a0201-mali-rgph5-census-special-review), [contribution](2018-12-04-iati-se-0-se-6-11793-11793a0101-mali-rgph5-population-census), [amendment](2018-12-04-iati-se-0-se-6-11793-11793a0103-mali-rgph5-census-agreement-amendment)). Those are commitment records rather than a census report: no enumeration date, publication or result is on file.

progress: Mixed, no open-data portal or single access-to-information law against a government monitoring system publishing its own completion rates
summary: There is [no open-data portal and no single access-to-information law](2026-04-01-evaluation-mise-en-oeuvre-loi-acces-information-mali), while a [government monitoring system](2026-07-29-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-30) publishes completion rates.
developments:
A 2026 evaluation found no single access-to-information law: the right is split across three statutes, and no open-data portal or policy is held ([evaluation](2026-04-01-evaluation-mise-en-oeuvre-loi-acces-information-mali)).

The government action monitoring and evaluation system published its first evaluation, covering the second half of 2025, and is operating and publishing completion rates ([system](2026-07-29-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-30)).

That first evaluation puts 43.43 per cent of planned activities completed, 109 of 251, with 83 in progress and 59 not started ([execution](2026-07-29-mali-conseil-des-ministres-cm-2026-30)). A state that publishes its own shortfall but has no open-data instrument is doing transparency by exception.

summary: A Chinese supplier [replaced a French one on the national biometric passport](2025-10-28 Mali Launches 'E-AES' Biometric Passport, Taps China's Emptech in Digital Sovereignty Move) in October 2025, a change officials cast as regained sovereignty.
developments:
The passport supplier changed from Idemia of France to Emptech of China, with officials framing it as regained sovereignty and local data management ([supplier](2025-10-28 Mali Launches 'E-AES' Biometric Passport, Taps China's Emptech in Digital Sovereignty Move)).

No contract value, term or data-hosting arrangement is published. It is the only Chinese engagement on record for the country, and it sits at the most sensitive point in the identity stack.

summary: There is [no dedicated 2025-2027 country programme](2026-08-10-mali-european-commission-country-page); the country is funded instead from a regional complex-settings allocation, with no digital activity named.
developments:
The Commission's country page states the country is funded from the central-Sahel complex-settings allocation for 2025 to 2027 rather than a dedicated country programme, against EUR 151m committed for 2021 to 2024 for growth and green economy and for human development and youth ([country page](2026-08-10-mali-european-commission-country-page)).

No digital or data-governance activity is named in either tranche, and no separate termination instrument was found, so what the base establishes is the disappearance of the country programme and not a decision to end digital cooperation.

summary: A Gulf operator's [US$6bn connectivity pledge](2024-03-01-niger-e-and-partner2connect-commitment-thenationalnews) for 2024 to 2026 names the country among sixteen markets, undivided between them.
developments:
The pledge was made to an international connectivity coalition in March 2024 across sixteen markets including Mali and Niger ([pledge](2024-03-01-niger-e-and-partner2connect-commitment-thenationalnews)).

It is not broken down by country, so no Mali-specific allocation, project or delivery can be established from it. No other Gulf instrument, investment or agreement is recorded for the country.

summary: A project on digital tools and citizen participation reached the stage of capitalising on what it has achieved ([report](2026-08-29-maliexpress-numerique-et-participation-citoyenne-le-projet-citoyens-20)).
developments: A project on digital tools and citizen participation reached the stage of capitalising on what it has achieved ([report](2026-08-29-maliexpress-numerique-et-participation-citoyenne-le-projet-citoyens-20)). No participation figure is stated.
